## Example 6.14 · Part (b) {#iv6-example-6-14-b .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .angles-lesson }

```{=html}
<p>Consider the points <span data-math="A(1,-1,3)"></span>, <span data-math="B(2,-4,5)"></span> and <span data-math="C(5,-13,11)"></span>.</p><p>b) Using vectors show that <span data-math="ABC"></span> is a straight line.</p><div data-module="reveal-panel" class="a-reveal"><button class="toggle-panel" aria-pressed="false">Show solution</button><div class="panel-answer" hidden><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{AB}=\begin{bmatrix}2-1\\-4+1\\5-3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\-3\\2\end{bmatrix}"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{BC}=\begin{bmatrix}5-2\\-13+4\\11-5\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\-9\\6\end{bmatrix}=3\overrightarrow{AB}"></span></div><p><span data-math="\overrightarrow{AB}"></span> and <span data-math="\overrightarrow{BC}"></span> have the same direction and meet at <span data-math="B"></span>. Therefore <span data-math="ABC"></span> is a straight line.</p></div></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Section 6 · p. 51</div>

::: notes
An equivalent solution uses AC=4AB, with common tail A. Retain the distinction between lengths in part (a) and directed vectors in part (b).
:::
